goal: Bind Kodi Bootstrap authorization to the exact verified installation scope, add revocation and truthful completion semantics, and preserve its existing bounded idempotent package workflow.
success_criteria: Bootstrap consent is independent of Android consent and bound to a canonical scope covering Bootstrap version, security-relevant manifest fields, and exact package-lock digest.
Bootstrap re-prompts after a scope change and provides a visible revoke action that blocks future application without deleting installed content.

Decline or revoked consent performs no package, configuration, add-on-enable, or skin mutation; failure never records applied_version; successful completion records it only after all required work succeeds.
All downloads, archive roots, IDs, versions, traversal, symlink, ABI, fixed settings, and fixed JSON-RPC operations remain allowlisted and tested.
Focused Kodi tests cover grant, decline, revoke, scope change, retry/idempotency, failure, and prohibited database, remote JSON-RPC, arbitrary built-in, and automated InstallFromZip approaches.
prohibited_actions: arbitrary paths, URLs, settings, built-ins, or JSON-RPC
primary_hypothesis: Replacing the indefinite installation_authorized boolean with a canonical scope-bound grant can preserve the existing Bootstrap workflow while forcing re-consent whenever its security-sensitive payload changes.
discriminating_check: Change one security-relevant scope input and verify Bootstrap blocks all mutation until fresh local consent, while an unchanged verified scope resumes idempotently and only records completion after success.
stop_conditions: The change would broaden Bootstrap beyond fixed verified packages, settings, IDs, or local in-process APIs.
A required behavior needs database access, remote JSON-RPC, arbitrary built-ins, InstallFromZip automation, or destructive rollback.
Implementation requires a secret, device mutation, deployment, release, or publication.
